newsitem.title: UK: UK offers no change on Falklands to Argentina.
newsitem.headline: UK offers no change on Falklands to Argentina.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government told Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella on Wednesday there would be no change in the British position on its sovereignty over the Falkland Islands.
The issue of the south Atlantic islands was brought up by di Tella during a 50-minute meeting with British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook described as useful by the Foreign Office.

Cook replied that "the British position on the fundamentals of Falkland Islands sovereignty and the islanders' right to self-determination is unchanged and we are not prepared to discuss the transfer or sharing of sovereignty", a Foreign Office spokesman said.
Argentina has claimed the islands which lie off its southern coast for more than 150 years. The former military junta seized them in 1982, triggering a war which ended in a British victory.

Before leaving Buenos Aires, di Tella had said he did not expect a change of policy in London over the Falklands following Labour's ending of the Conservatives' 18 years in power at the May 1 election.
The spokesman said Cook and di Tella agreed that relations between the two countries were in good shape and underpinned by booming trade and increased investment by British companies in Argentina.

They noted "encouraging progress" following the 1995 agreement on oil exploration in the south Atlantic. Cook told di Tella that he and the Falkland islanders would welcome a long-term agreement governing fishing rights around the islands.
